newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: Bond yields broke key technical levels in busy trade which left the market on a cautiously bullish footing on Thursday, dealers said.
At the local finish, the key R150 stock was pegged at a 15.30 percent yield from 15.41 percent overnight, while Eskom's 168 was at 15.455 percent from 15.48 percent previously.
The market's gains were initially spurred by the release late on Wednesday of data showing money supply growth rose a better-than-expected 14.69 percent in July from a revised 15.74 percent in June.
The R150 was already heading towards its intraday low of 15.26 percent when data showing South Africa's trade account swelled to a 2.58 billion rand surplus in July was released.
The surplus compared with a 27 million rand deficit in June and was more than three times higher than economists most optimistic forecast of an 800 million rand surplus.

Standard Bank Economics Division said the 55.2 percent month-on-month rise in exports to 13.7 billion rand could be partly attributed to a revision in June's "unclassified" category -- mainly arms, platinum and uranium. This category showed a 1.75 billion rand turnaround in July from June.
While most import categories grew, the most significant growth was 811.4 million rand growth in machinery imports and 505.9 million rand growth in transport equipment imports.
Traders said the figure had stunned the market, but that combined with the money supply data overnight, had created a more bullish scenario.
Technical levels had been broken on the way down, notably the 15.32 percent level, which a dealer said had put the market on a "cautiously bullish" footing.
"The 15.19 percent level is the next one and from there we can go as low as 14.80 percent on the charts," the dealer said.
He noted that there had been some foreign buying in the afternoon session, reversing a trend of selling in recent days.
Weakness on the U.S. Treasury bond market, where the yield on the benchmark 30-year stock was back above seven percent at 7.03 percent, had little impact.
On the currency market, steady local importer demand for dollars as well as short-covering throughout the day left the rand slightly weaker but off its worst level.
It was last quoted at 4.5080/5130 from 4.5050/5100 on Wednesday.
"We've seen good demand for dollars all day," a dealer said, noting that players were looking to take advantage of higher carry points with the New York market being closed on Monday for Labour Day.
Against the crosses, the rand was last at 7.0197/0320 on sterling from 7.0226/0349 on Wednesday and at 0.3278/3284 marks from 0.3271/3277 marks previously.

Bond Exchange figures showed foreigners were net sellers of 98.42 million rand of South African bonds on Wednesday after selling 101.45 million on Tuesday. Nominal cumulative volumes were pegged at 6.87 billion rand on Wednesday.

On the money market, three-month NCDs were lower at between 16.50 and 16.65 percent from 16.55 to 16.70 percent on Wednesday, while 90-day BAs were also softer at between 15.90 and 16.05 percent from 16.00 and 16.10 percent previously.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage surged to 9.208 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.705 billion rand on Tuesday.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom, +27 11 482-1003
